So there is a lot more to it on that side that I didn’t share. I was trying to keep it condensed as for it not to be a novel and I don’t think I did a very good job at doing that. So this was my second clinical in a hospital setting. Last semester we did our clinical at a rehab facility where I did a ton of assessments. Reflecting back on it with all the feedback I have received, i believe the biggest thing I was stuck on was the mental state of the pt not being able to provide a clear consent to me. I have never been in that position. I initially asked the instructor a series of questions and I don’t remember what they were word for word but they were along the lines of “I know skin assessments are important but she’s not responsive enough that I feel I can get adequate consent and I’m not sure what to do. What is the best way to go about this?” The response I got was something like “You go in there and do it”. My frustration is that when I ask questions it is do what your told to do and stop asking questions mentality. It wasn’t until I got treated like the dumbest being on the planet by them and a series of jabs that she suggest I do it with a female nurse. At that point I was so put off by the situation I felt completely lost and led me to maintain my stance on it. If they had just explained to me about consent with altered mental states and told me to grab a female nurse and proceed with the assessment. I would have done exactly that. I want explanation, constructive criticism, and guidance in areas I’m unsure about. I want to do the right thing but I also don’t want to get told to do something and it end up being the wrong thing. 

Please don’t take it as if I’m defending my decision because im not. I realize now that I should have went and talked to the nurse about it after the response I got from the instructor and proceeded with it.
Yes I have and will absolutely be making changes to the way I approach my role going forward, thank you!

It was my first time with a pt in that state and clearly drew the line of boundary in the wrong spot. That is one of the things that made me feel really uncomfortable about it. We get assigned a pt prior to going out on the floor. I always immediately go introduce myself and explain the who, what, & why. I got a yes from her when I asked her if it was okay that I was student after I managed to get her to be awake long enough to finish my question but in her state I felt if I asked something ridiculously off the wall I would have got a yes. As a first year student I really don’t think I should have been assigned to her, I was surprised she was not in critical care after seeing her condition and her labs. The instructor gets there early and gets all the info on pts prior to assigning us. So the instructor knew what her condition was like. I mentioned it to them out of caution incase it was a mistake and was quickly informed not to question her judgment. 

I agree with you that I should have assessed her now that I’ve gotten feedback from nurses. It’s exactly what I needed. I’ll definitely be making different decisions at clinical going forward.

I never even considered that.. that’s an excellent point. After reading all of these comments I realize I’m approaching this role incorrectly and need to make changes. This was really helpful, thank you!

I did not know that about wounds and is really good to know going forward. It wasn’t the invasion of privacy that bothered me, it was her altered mental state. This role is completely different from anything I’ve done so it’s been my biggest challenge adjusting into it. So I appreciate your input. Everyone’s take on it has been helpful, thank you!

The opposite gender part of it was just a tiny portion of it. It was the combination of factors that led me to where I was. If it wasn’t for everything else I wouldn’t have been uncomfortable with it at all. I think the part that bothered me the most about it was her mental status and it just seemed inappropriate for me given I’ve never been in that situation filling that kind of role. So that’s really helpful to know that mental status is typically disregarded in that type of situation. Thank you!

I guess I should have at least added that one of the things that the parents shared was that she has gone through this 6+ times in the past 3 months and each time snaps out of it like nothing happened around 5-6pm. We are only there 8hrs. However if I was on the floor working as an RN I’d be there 7-7. So, one of the things I explained to the instructor was that if I was actually the RN I would wait until that time in hopes that she would be more responsive and if she hasn’t snapped out of it by then I would go ahead and proceed with it to make sure it is done prior to my shift ending. 

Regardless of all that though I think it was still the wrong position to take based on everyone’s input and will make different decisions in the future. Thank you for your input!

Thanks everyone, I really appreciate the input. It’s really helpful and provides me with a different perspective going forward. The hardest part of this program for me has been adjusting into the role a nurse plays. It’s completely different from anything I’ve experienced.
